info.title: Workflow Service
info.description:
Workflow orchestration service. Create DAG workflows, modify them, and execute them by slug with runtime inputs.

## Quick Start

**Step 1 — Create a workflow:**
```
POST /workflows
{ "featureSlug": "my-feature", "dag": { "nodes": [...], "edges": [...] } }
```

**Step 2 — Execute by slug (each time an event occurs):**
```
POST /workflows/by-slug/my-feature-obsidian/execute
{ "inputs": { "email": "user@example.com" } }
```
Returns a run ID. Poll `GET /workflow-runs/{id}` for status and result.

**Step 3 — Modify the workflow (metadata or DAG):**
```
PUT /workflows/{id}
{ "dag": { "nodes": [...], "edges": [...] } }
```
If the DAG structure changed, a new workflow is created (fork). The response tells you what happened via `_action`.

## DAG Format

A DAG has `nodes` (steps) and `edges` (execution order).

**Recommended node type: `http.call`** — calls any microservice by name:
```json
{
  "id": "create-user",
  "type": "http.call",
  "config": { "service": "client", "method": "POST", "path": "/users" },
  "inputMapping": { "body": "$ref:flow_input.userData" }
}
```
The service name maps to env vars `{NAME}_SERVICE_URL` and `{NAME}_SERVICE_API_KEY`.
To discover available services and their endpoints, use the API Registry.

## Input Mapping ($ref syntax)

Use `inputMapping` to pass data between nodes:
- `$ref:flow_input.field` — from the workflow execution inputs
- `$ref:node-id.output.field` — from a previous node's output

## Features

- Automatic retries (3 attempts, 5s apart) on each node
- Async execution with status polling
- Topological ordering — nodes run in dependency order
- Native constructs: `wait` (delay), `condition` (branching), `for-each` (loops)

## Per-App Secrets (BYOK)

Some services (e.g. Stripe) require per-app API keys. **Never pass secrets as workflow inputs.**
Instead, use the **key-service** app-keys system:

**1. Register the key once (at app startup via `instrumentation.ts`):**
```
POST key-service /internal/app-keys
{ "appId": "my-app", "provider": "stripe", "apiKey": "sk_live_xxx" }
```

**2. Pass `appId` (not the secret) in your workflow inputs:**
```
POST /workflows/by-name/create-course/execute
{ "appId": "my-app", "inputs": { "courseName": "My Course", "price": 99 } }
```

**3. The downstream service resolves the key itself:**
The service (e.g. stripe-service) receives `appId`, calls key-service
`GET /internal/app-keys/stripe/decrypt?appId=my-app` to get the decrypted key.
No secret ever transits through the workflow.

## Setup Pattern (Next.js `instrumentation.ts`)

Put all one-time setup in your app's `instrumentation.ts`:
```typescript
export async function register() {
  // Register per-app secrets
  await fetch(`${KEY_SERVICE_URL}/internal/app-keys`, {
    method: "POST",
    headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json", "x-api-key": KEY_SERVICE_API_KEY },
    body: JSON.stringify({ appId: "my-app", provider: "stripe", apiKey: STRIPE_SECRET_KEY }),
  });
  // Create or update workflows via POST /workflows or PUT /workflows/{id}
}
```

featureSlug.description: Feature slug from features-service. Used for naming and feature-level grouping.

humanId.description: Human ID if this workflow was generated in a human expert's style.

workflowSlug.description: Unique technical identifier. Use this to execute via /workflows/by-slug/{workflowSlug}/execute.

workflowDynastySlug.description: Stable lineage slug (constant across all versions of a dynasty). Use for dynasty-level grouping.

workflowDynastyName.description: Stable lineage display name (constant across all versions of a dynasty).

signature.description: Deterministic SHA-256 hash of the canonical DAG JSON. Changes when any node, edge, or config changes.

workflowDynastySignatureName.description: Star name of this lineage, lowercase (e.g. 'vega'; 'bright-vega' once a feature has burned every single IAU star name). Lineages created before 2026-10-10 keep their older word (e.g. 'sequoia'). Set once at lineage creation. Unique among all workflows (any status, any org) within the same featureSlug.

version.description: Version number within the lineage. Starts at 1.

contentModel.description: The chat-service model alias this workflow writes its content with (e.g. 'flash', 'deepseek-pro', 'fable'), read from the `model` field of the DAG's content-generation POST /generate request body. Derived at read from the DAG, so a consumer can label a workflow row without downloading and parsing the DAG. Null when the workflow makes no content-generation call, when the call does not state a model (content-generation then applies its own default), when the value is produced at run time by another node, or when several content-generation calls state different models — never a guess.

contentPromptType.description: The content-generation prompt template this workflow renders (e.g. 'cold-email'), read from the `type` field of the DAG's content-generation POST /generate request body. Same derivation and same null cases as `contentModel`.

contentTemplateDynasty.description: TPL-DYNASTY-1021-WF: the content-generation template DYNASTY this workflow writes with. Every run reads the dynasty's CURRENT head (GET /internal/template-dynasties/{slug}/head), so a new head version reaches it with no new workflow version; `contentPromptType` is then the head the DAG was last written against. Null when the workflow pins a template version.

writesWithLegBest.description: BEST-TPL-LLM-1022: true when the workflow states no template and no LLM: every run writes with the template dynasty and the LLM features-service ranks best on the workflow's leg (lowest $/outcome, narrowed by the campaign strategy's tactics). `contentModel`, `contentPromptType` and `contentTemplateDynasty` are then null: what wrote each email is recorded per generation by content-generation.

status.description: Per-version lifecycle status. Only active workflows can be executed. Within a dynasty the latest version is 'active' and predecessors are 'deprecated'. Set on demand via PUT /workflows/{id}/status. Distinct from `workflowDynastyStatus`.

workflowDynastyStatus.description: Dynasty-level status. 'deprecated' means the entire lineage is retired: no version of it can be executed (execute returns 410) and it is not listed as an active candidate. Constant across all versions of a dynasty. Set via PUT /workflows/dynasty/{workflowDynastySlug}/status.

creationType.description: How this workflow was created: 'scratch' = brand-new dynasty, 'upgrade' = new version of an existing dynasty, 'fork' = forked from another workflow.

createdFromWorkflow.description: ID of the workflow this one was derived from (predecessor for 'upgrade', source for 'fork'). Null for 'scratch'.

createdByUserId.description: User ID that created this workflow.

createdByRunId.description: Run ID that created this workflow.

WorkflowCategory.description: Legacy provenance tag (pre-2026-10-10). The generator no longer sets it: the pipe link lives in features-service (/internal/workflow-leg-assignments).

WorkflowChannel.description: Legacy provenance tag (pre-2026-10-10). The generator no longer sets it: the pipe link lives in features-service (/internal/workflow-leg-assignments).

WorkflowAudienceType.description: Legacy provenance tag (pre-2026-10-10). The generator no longer sets it: the pipe link lives in features-service (/internal/workflow-leg-assignments).

reason.description: Why this workflow was deprecated, in plain words. 'Not specified' for workflows deprecated before 2026-10-20 (the reason was never recorded).

decidedBy.description: Who decided it: a staff email, 'workflow-service' for an automatic deprecation (an upgrade replacing this version), or 'user:<id>' when only the caller's user id is known. Null when unknown (every pre-2026-10-20 'Not specified' row).

decidedAt.description: ISO instant the deprecation was decided. Null when unknown (pre-2026-10-20 'Not specified' rows).

WorkflowDeprecation.description: Why, by whom and when this workflow was deprecated. Null while it is executable (status AND workflowDynastyStatus 'active'). A retired dynasty carries its retirement decision on every version; a version replaced by an upgrade says so.

createdForBrandId.description: Optional brand ID — records which brand context created this workflow.

subrequestId.description: Optional subrequest ID for cost tracking.

description.description: Human-readable description of what this workflow does.

featureSlug.description: Feature slug from features-service. Required — used to build the workflow slug/name and for feature-level grouping.

pipeId.description: The features-service pipe the workflow runs on, `<channel slug>|<leg key>`. Read from the catalogue: it must exist, its channel must equal featureSlug and it must be platform-worked (else 422). The workflow is then registered on that pipe in features-service (POST /internal/workflow-leg-assignments/register, active at once), which owns the link; this service stores no pipe.

tags.description: Free-form tags for filtering/grouping (e.g. channels used in the DAG: ["email", "linkedin"]).

nodes.description: The steps of the workflow. Must contain at least one node.

edges.description: Execution order between nodes. Empty array for single-node workflows.

onError.description: Node ID of an error handler that runs when any node in the DAG fails (including validateResponse failures). Auto-injected parameters (available as script params, no inputMapping needed): failedNodeId (string) — the module ID of the step that failed; errorMessage (string) — the error message text. Can also access outputs from previously completed nodes via $ref syntax. Use this to call end-run with success: false. Tip: check errorMessage to distinguish expected stops (e.g. 'validation failed: expected found=true') from real errors.

forkedForPipe.description: The pipe (`<channel>|<leg>`) a one-leg copy was forked for (`POST /workflows/{id}/fork` with `pipeId`). Inert at run time: it only makes two copies of the same steps two workflows, one per pipe (a workflow sits on ONE leg, owner 2026-10-19). Which pipe a workflow serves is features-service's, never read from here. An upgrade that states none keeps its predecessor's.

id.description: Unique identifier for this node within the DAG. Used in edges and $ref input mappings.

type.description: Node type. Must be one of the registered types — unknown strings are rejected (no silent fallback). Preferred: "http.call" — call any microservice. config requires { service, method, path }. Inline JS: "script" — runs node.config.code (string) inline as a Windmill rawscript. config = { code: string, language?: "bun" | "deno" }. Inputs via inputMapping, outputs via `return { … }`. Native flow control: "condition" — if/then/else branching (uses Windmill branchone). Outgoing edges with 'condition' define branches; nodes downstream of a conditional edge are nested inside that branch. Outgoing edges without 'condition' define after-branch steps that always execute. "wait" — sleep/delay. "for-each" — loop over items (body nodes are nested inside the loop). Legacy named types: stripe.createProduct, client.createUser, transactional-email.send.

config.description: Static parameters passed to the node. For http.call: { service, method, path, body?, query?, headers? }. For script: { code (string, required, inline JS), language? ("bun" | "deno", default "bun") }. For wait: { seconds }. For for-each: { iterator, parallel?, skipFailures? }. Each key becomes a direct parameter of the underlying script. Special config keys (stripped before passing to script): retries (number) — override default retry count; validateResponse ({ field, equals }) — throw error if response[field] !== equals, triggers onError handler; stopAfterIf (string) — native Windmill stop_after_if. JS expression evaluated after step completes using 'result' variable, stops the entire flow gracefully (no onError, no subsequent steps) when true. Example: "result.found == false". For conditional branching (run some steps but not others), use a "condition" node instead; skipIf (string) — native Windmill skip_if. JS expression evaluated before this step runs, skips only this step when true. Can reference previous results via results.<module_id>. Example: "results.fetch_lead.found == false". For multi-step skipping, prefer a "condition" node.

inputMapping.description: Dynamic input references using $ref syntax. Use "$ref:flow_input.fieldName" for workflow execution inputs, or "$ref:node-id.output.fieldName" for a previous node's output. Keys in inputMapping override same-named keys in config.

retries.description: Number of retry attempts on failure. Defaults to 3 if omitted. Set to 0 for non-idempotent operations (e.g., sending emails, consuming queue items) to prevent duplicates.

from.description: Source node ID — this node runs first.

to.description: Target node ID — runs after the source completes.

condition.description: JavaScript expression for conditional branching. Only used when source node is type "condition". Edges WITH condition: target node (and its chain) are nested inside that branch — they only execute when the condition is true. Edges WITHOUT condition from a condition node: target is an after-branch step that always executes. Expressions can reference previous results (results.<module_id>.<field>) or flow_input. Example: "results.fetch_lead.found == true"

description.description: What this workflow does, in plain words.

siblingLine.description: WF-SHORT-LINE-1023, display only: a fragment of at most 10 words saying ONLY what sets this workflow's dynasty apart from the other workflows on the same pipe (never the pipe, leg or channel, a template, an LLM, a version or a date). Null when the dynasty is the only workflow on its pipe, when its pipe's lines are not written yet (at most ~10 min after a change), or when it sits on several pipes with different lines (read `siblingLines`).

siblingLines.description: The dynasty's line per pipe it sits on (features-service leg assignments, any state), one entry per leg; empty when none is written.

status.description: Per-version lifecycle: active (latest of its dynasty) or deprecated.

workflowDynastyStatus.description: Whole-lineage status: deprecated = retired, never runs.

contentModel.description: Model of the content-generation call, derived from the DAG; null when it states none.

contentPromptType.description: Prompt template of the content-generation call, derived from the DAG; null when it states none.

contentTemplateDynasty.description: Template dynasty the workflow writes with (its live head each run); null when it pins a template version.

writesWithLegBest.description: True when the workflow states no template and no LLM: each run writes with its leg's best (features-service).

workflowDynastySlug.description: The dynasty slug whose status was set.

status.description: The dynasty's status after the write.

updatedWorkflows.description: How many version rows in the lineage carry the new status.

activeWorkflowSlug.description: The workflow slug left executable. Null when the dynasty was retired — a retired dynasty has no executable version, and nothing is substituted for it.

status.description: New dynasty-level status. 'deprecated' retires the entire lineage: no version of it can be executed any more (every execute returns 410) and it stops being listed as an active candidate. 'active' un-retires it. Idempotent — re-applying the same status is a no-op success (re-deprecating with a new `reason` records the new reason).

reason.description: REQUIRED when deprecating (DEPRECATION-REASON-1020): why, in plain words a staff member reads months later. A deprecation without one is refused with 400 `deprecation_reason_required`. Ignored when activating.

decidedBy.description: Who decided (staff email). Absent = the caller's x-email header, else 'user:<x-user-id>'.

deprecatedVersions.description: Merge: how many absorbed versions were deprecated.

restoredVersions.description: Un-merge: how many versions were restored to their exact prior state.

absorbedDynastySlug.description: The dynasty merged away (deprecated on both axes while the merge is open).

survivorDynastySlug.description: The dynasty it was merged into.

finalSurvivorDynastySlug.description: The survivor through every open merge (A into B into C = C); null once un-merged.

legKeys.description: The pipe (leg keys on featureSlug) both dynasties served when merged.

unmergedAt.description: Null while the merge is open.

intoWorkflowDynastySlug.description: The SURVIVOR dynasty: same channel and same pipe (features-service leg assignments), executable.

reason.description: Why (required), e.g. 'Same template dynasty and same model on the same pipe'.

decidedBy.description: Who decided (staff email). Absent = the caller's x-email header, else 'user:<x-user-id>'.
Who decided (staff email). Absent = the caller's x-email header, else 'user:<x-user-id>'.

workflowSlug.description: The version that was running (the dynasty's active version).

legKeys.description: Only when `legKey` was sent: the legs features-service has this dynasty ACTIVE on (exactly [legKey]).

workflows.description: Every workflow (dynasty) running the template or model (on the pipe, when `legKey` was sent): retired, or that would be on a dry run.

retired.description: Dynasties retired by this call (0 on a dry run).

legKeys.description: Every leg it is ACTIVE on: `legKey` and at least one other.

keptOnOtherLegs.description: Only when `legKey` was sent: dynasties running the template or model on that leg AND another one, never retired by a per-pipe call.

promptType.description: content-generation template type: retire every runnable workflow whose content call PINS it. A workflow writing with a template dynasty's live head is never retired by one of that dynasty's versions (TPL-DYNASTY-1021-WF3).

model.description: Writer model alias: retire every runnable workflow whose content call writes with it.

featureSlug.description: Narrow to one channel. Absent = every channel.

legKey.description: Narrow to ONE pipe (`featureSlug` x `legKey`, e.g. lead_found_to_website_visit; requires `featureSlug`): only dynasties features-service has ACTIVE on that leg are listed/retired, each with its `legKeys`. A matching dynasty also active on another leg of the channel is never retired (it would stop that pipe too): it is listed under `keptOnOtherLegs`. Absent = every leg, answered as before (RETIRE-BY-CONTENT-PER-LEG-1023).

dryRun.description: true = list what would be retired, write nothing (the confirmation a staff member reads first).

reason.description: Why these workflows are retired (DEPRECATION-REASON-1020). Absent = 'Uses deprecated template <promptType>' / 'Uses deprecated model <model>'.

decidedBy.description: Who decided (staff email). Absent = the caller's x-email header, else 'user:<x-user-id>'.

status.description: New per-version lifecycle status. 'deprecated' retires THIS version only: it can no longer be executed by id, and it stops being the dynasty's execution target when resolving by slug. 'active' restores it — rejected with 409 when another version of the same dynasty is already active. Idempotent (re-deprecating with a new `reason` records the new reason).

reason.description: REQUIRED when deprecating (DEPRECATION-REASON-1020): why, in plain words a staff member reads months later. A deprecation without one is refused with 400 `deprecation_reason_required`. Ignored when activating.

decidedBy.description: Who decided (staff email). Absent = the caller's x-email header, else 'user:<x-user-id>'.

status.description: Dynasty status ('active' | 'deprecated'). On the list surface this field reflects the item's DYNASTY status (mirrors `workflowDynastyStatus`) so the dashboard can render one active/deprecated flag per dynasty row. (On the single-workflow GET /workflows/{id} surface, `status` is the per-version lifecycle status instead.)

requiredProviders.description: Providers required by this workflow (with domain info for logo lookup). Empty array if the workflow has no http.call nodes. Computed via a single deduped key-service POST per list request, so callers no longer need to fan out N follow-up requests to /workflows/{id}/required-providers.

domain.description: Provider's primary domain for logo lookup (e.g. 'anthropic.com'). Null if unknown.

endpoints.description: The http.call endpoints extracted from the workflow DAG.

providers.description: Providers required by this workflow, with domain info for logo lookup.

_action.description: What happened: 'updated' means the existing workflow was modified in-place (metadata or same-signature DAG). 'forked' means a new workflow was created with a new lineage because the DAG signature changed.

_forkedFromWorkflowName.description: Present only when _action='forked'. The display name of the original workflow that was forked.

_forkedFromId.description: Present only when _action='forked'. The ID of the original workflow that was forked.

example.description: Cold outreach sequence for PR campaigns

existingWorkflowId.description: ID of the existing workflow that already has this DAG signature.

existingWorkflowSlug.description: Workflow slug of the existing workflow that already has this DAG signature.

allOf.description: Optional new DAG. When omitted, only metadata (description, tags) is updated in-place. When provided with the same structural signature, the DAG is updated in-place. When provided with a different structural signature, a new workflow is created (fork) and the original is kept active (unless its lineage has zero campaign runs, in which case it is deprecated).

invalidEndpoints.description: http.call endpoints that do not exist in the corresponding service's current OpenAPI spec.

fieldIssues.description: Body/output field mismatches between http.call nodes and the current OpenAPI specs.

templateRefs.description: Content-generation template references found in the DAG.

issues.description: Variable mismatches between workflow and prompt templates.

templateContract.description: Template contract validation result. Present when content-generation service is reachable.

templateType.description: Prompt template type used by this node.

variablesProvided.description: Variable names the workflow provides to this node.

nodeId.description: DAG node ID that calls content-generation.

id.description: Run UUID. Use this to poll status via GET /workflow-runs/{id}.

brandIds.description: Brand IDs associated with this run. Multi-brand campaigns produce multiple IDs.

featureSlug.description: Feature slug from features-service. Used for per-feature analytics.

workflowSlug.description: Slug of the workflow that was executed. Use this to re-execute via /workflows/by-slug/{workflowSlug}/execute.

userId.description: User ID from the execution context.

runId.description: Runs-service run ID for this execution (auto-created).

executionKey.description: Deterministic key used to prevent duplicate active executions.

conflictPolicy.description: Conflict policy used when this run was reserved.

inputs.description: The inputs that were passed at execution time.

result.description: Workflow result (available when status is completed). Contains the output of the last node.

error.description: Error message (available when status is failed). Raw Windmill error — use errorSummary for a clean version.

message.description: Clean error message with stack traces stripped.

flowStatus.description: Windmill flow_status object. Contains per-module execution details including resolved inputs, outputs, and timing for each step in the flow.

featureSlug.description: Feature slug used to build the name.

signature.description: SHA-256 hash of the canonical DAG JSON.

workflowDynastySignatureName.description: Star name of this lineage (older lineages keep their pre-2026-10-10 word).

mode.description: proactive: the workflow finds its own people. reactive: a trigger hands them over.

triggerId.description: The trigger of a reactive pipe (features-service); null on a proactive one.

toStep.description: The step the pipe produces: the workflow's ROI is that step's value over what a run costs.

pipe.description: The pipe as the generator read it from the features-service catalogue on THIS call, and the one the dynasty is now assigned to there (features-service owns the link). Null when the call ran no generation (client-supplied DAG).

action.description: What happened: 'created' = new dynasty inserted (creation_type='scratch'), 'existing' = matching active workflow already exists with same signature, 'updated' = upgrade with same signature applied in-place, 'upgraded' = new version inserted in same dynasty (creation_type='upgrade').

description.description: Natural-language description of the desired workflow.

featureSlug.description: The workflow's channel slug in features-service (e.g. 'sales-cold-email-outreach'). Required: it names the workflow and its pipes are the ones the workflow can run on.

pipeId.description: The features-service pipe the workflow runs on, `<channel slug>|<leg key>` (GET /internal/catalogue/pipes). Its channel slug must equal featureSlug. Omit it when the channel has one pipe, or to let the generator pick the pipe the description is about.

services.description: Scope generation to these services. Reduces prompt size and improves accuracy.

nodeTypes.description: Suggest specific node types for the LLM to use.

expectedInputs.description: Expected flow_input field names (e.g. campaignId, email).

workflowDynastySlug.description: Stable dynasty slug (constant across all versions of the dynasty). The route resolves it to the currently-active row, so callers do not need to track which version is active after prior upgrades.

description.description: Natural-language description of the desired upgraded workflow. Required when `dag` is not provided (LLM regenerates the DAG from this description). Optional when `dag` is provided; if present, replaces the stored description on the resulting row.

allOf.description: Optional client-supplied DAG. When provided, the LLM is not invoked: the DAG is validated, its signature computed, and the upgrade applies the same in-place / new-version branching as the LLM path. category/channel/audienceType are inherited from the existing row. Use this to apply surgical fixes to a workflow (e.g. patch a single script node) without re-running generation. Either `dag` or `description` MUST be provided.

pipeId.description: The features-service pipe to regenerate for, `<channel slug>|<leg key>`. Defaults to the pipe features-service assigns the dynasty to when it is exactly one; otherwise the generator resolves it from featureSlug. Ignored when `dag` is provided.

allOf.description: Optional hints to guide generation. Ignored when `dag` is provided.

status.description: Per-version lifecycle status: active or deprecated.

workflowDynastyStatus.description: Dynasty-level status. 'deprecated' means the whole lineage is retired and cannot execute, whatever this row's per-version `status` says. A row is executable only when both are 'active'.

createdForBrandId.description: Brand ID this workflow was created for, or null.

upgradedTo.description: ID of the active workflow this one was upgraded to, computed from successor lineage. Null when this is the active row or no successor was found in the result set.

createdAt.description: ISO instant this version row was created. Reliable: set once at insert, never moved by a later edit. A version is executable from this instant unless it was born under a retired dynasty (then `executableUntil` equals it).

executableUntil.description: ISO instant this version STOPPED being executable (its version status became 'deprecated' or its dynasty was retired), the earliest such transition. Null while the version is executable (status AND workflowDynastyStatus 'active'); cleared again if the version is re-activated, so it reports only the LAST stretch (an older stop/restart gap is not kept). To know whether a dynasty could run at instant T: one of its versions has createdAt <= T and (executableUntil null or > T). How reliable it is: see `executableUntilSource`.

executableUntilSource.description: Where `executableUntil` comes from. 'recorded': written by this service at the transition (every stop since 2026-10-19), exact. Two active dynasties on the same pipe writing with the same template dynasty and model are one workflow: this absorbs `workflowDynastySlug` into `intoWorkflowDynastySlug`. **DAG with same signature**: the DAG structure hasn't changed (e.g. only config tweaks that don't affect the hash). Updates in-place. Returns `_action: 'updated'`.

**DAG with new signature**: creates a new workflow in a new lineage (fork). The original workflow is kept active unless its entire lineage has zero campaign runs, in which case it is deprecated. Returns `_action: 'forked'` with the new workflow data, plus `_forkedFromName`, `_forkedFromId`, and `_sourceDynastyDeprecated` to indicate what happened to the source lineage.

The new workflow's ID is in the response — use it going forward. Returns 201 for forks, 200 for in-place updates.

post.description: General capability for any workflow (an `http.call` node). Works out which figures `question` needs and reads them at run time: PUBLIC figures (our public catalogue routes, the live web) and the figures of the organization(s) the RECIPIENT belongs to, read through the customer API gateway as that recipient, with no staff access. A figure that cannot be read is named in `missing`; the caller decides what to do (the AI Follow-up Email workflow sends nothing). The model spend is declared by chat-service on the calling run.
